prompt: The lesson gives a second definition of armor. Which of the following is it?
options: A method of conducting fire and maneuver
A defensive covering that affords protection
A group of vehicles that supports infantry by direct fire
A unit that performs reconnaissance and provides security
explanation: Page 13 defines armor both as a combined arms force for mounted combat and as a defensive covering that affords protection.

prompt: Which statement about the doctrinal armor mission is correct?
options: Armor may conduct ISO activities only while attached to an infantry unit, never independently
Armor conducts ISO activities only in wartime, when ordered by the division commander
Armor may also conduct ISO activities, independently or as part of a task force, in a peacetime environment as required by higher headquarters
Armor is limited to ISO activities in a peacetime environment, and its mission excludes closing with the enemy
explanation: Page 14 says armor may also conduct ISO activities, independently or as part of a task force, in a peacetime environment as required by higher headquarters. Its doctrinal mission still includes closing with and neutralizing enemy forces.

prompt: Which list contains the characteristics of armor?
options: Armor protection, firepower, mobility, amphibious capability, intensive and flexible communication, shock action
Armor protection, firepower, mobility, flexibility, air transportability, shock action
Armor protection, firepower, mobility, flexibility, intensive and flexible communication, shock action
Armor protection, firepower, mobility, flexibility, intensive and flexible communication, logistics independence
explanation: Page 20 lists six characteristics: armor protection, firepower, mobility, flexibility, intensive and flexible communication, and shock action. Amphibious and air transportable are features of particular vehicles (page 73), not characteristics of armor.

prompt: An armor task force halts its attack to the north and blocks an enemy moving in from the east without pausing to reorganize. This mainly describes which characteristic of armor?
options: Mobility
Flexibility
Shock action
Firepower
explanation: Page 21 lists flexibility as a characteristic of armor; changing task and direction without reorganizing is what it describes. Movement, impact and fire are needed in any block but are not what the sudden change of mission tests.

prompt: What is the total strength of the mechanized infantry company shown in the lesson's organization chart?
options: 5 officers and 111 enlisted
4 officers and 126 enlisted
6 officers and 126 enlisted
5 officers and 126 enlisted
explanation: Page 24 shows the company at 5 officers and 126 enlisted: a headquarters of 2 and 15 plus three platoons of 1 and 37.

prompt: According to the lesson's chart, a mechanized infantry platoon has 1 officer and how many enlisted?
explanation: Page 25 shows the platoon at 1 officer and 37 enlisted: a headquarters of 1 and 10 plus three squads of 9. Page 27 confirms the four AIFVs.

prompt: Which statement describes the dismount team of a mechanized infantry squad?
options: The carrier team leader, gunner and driver
Only the squad leader and the automatic rifleman
The platoon headquarters section
All squad members who are not part of the carrier team
explanation: Page 26 says the dismount team is made up of all squad members not part of the carrier team. The carrier team leader, gunner and driver form the carrier team.

prompt: Which pair of tasks is performed by mechanized infantry MOUNTED and DISMOUNTED, respectively?
options: Fix the enemy to allow maneuver; destroy light armor vehicles
Destroy light armor vehicles; fix the enemy to allow maneuver
Secure terrain; assault unprepared, suppressed defenses
Infiltrate enemy positions; move over terrain not trafficable by vehicles
explanation: Page 28 lists destroying light armor vehicles as a mounted capability, and page 29 lists fixing the enemy to allow maneuver as a dismounted one. The other pairs are both mounted or both dismounted.

prompt: The AVs of the mechanized infantry are restricted to certain avenues of approach due to:
options: Limitations in the terrain
Insufficient time to mount and dismount
Vulnerability to small arms and indirect fire
Dependence on flatbeds for deployment
explanation: Page 30 says AVs are restricted to certain avenues of approach due to limitation in the terrain.

prompt: Which of the following is NOT an SOP on dismounting?
options: Avoid piling up at the door of the AV
No riders on top of the AV
Move inside the AV one at a time
Never hide behind an AV
explanation: Page 31 lists the dismounting SOPs, including avoiding piling up at the door, no riders on top and never hiding behind an AV. Moving inside one at a time is a mounting SOP (page 45).

prompt: Dismount right is prescribed when there is no enemy contact and:
options: The terrain is not favorable on the right
The enemy fires from the left
A fast dismount is necessary
The terrain is not favorable on the left
explanation: Pages 33 and 34 give dismount right when there is no enemy contact and the terrain is not favorable on the left. A need for a fast dismount is the standard dismount (page 32).

prompt: Which of the following describes the conditions for the standard dismount?
options: No enemy contact, and the terrain is not favorable on the left
No enemy contact, and the terrain is not favorable on the right
No enemy contact yet, the terrain is favorable, and a fast dismount is necessary
Enemy contact from the left, and a fast dismount is necessary
explanation: Page 32 gives the standard dismount for no enemy contact yet, favorable terrain and a necessary fast dismount. Pages 33 and 34 give dismount left or right when the terrain is not favorable.

prompt: Which pair lists the limitations of cavalry?
options: High logistics requirements; dependence on flatbeds for deployment
High logistics requirements; mobility restricted by dense forest, steep rugged terrain and major water obstacles
Lack of organic transport for Classes III, V and IX; mobility restricted in extremely close terrain
Inability to operate in an economy of force role without reinforcement; high logistics requirements
explanation: Page 61 lists high logistics requirements and mobility restricted by dense forest, steep rugged terrain and major water obstacles. Flatbeds, Classes III, V and IX and close terrain are tank limitations (pages 67-68), and cavalry can operate in economy of force without reinforcement (page 60).

prompt: Which of the following describes the separate cavalry troop/company?
options: It is organized as part of an armored division and is always heavy
It is organized as part of separate light and armored brigades, and is heavy or light according to the brigade
It operates for the division commander in any operational environment
It is organized as part of the air cavalry squadron and is always light
explanation: Page 59 says the separate cavalry troop is organized as part of separate light and armored brigades, is heavy or light depending on the brigade, and operates for the brigade commander.

prompt: Which statement describes cavalry's economy of force role?
options: It lets the cavalry take over the main attack so the main body can avoid engagement
It lets the commander conserve the combat power of divisions or brigades for engagement where he desires
It lets the cavalry hold all key terrain permanently so no reserve is required
It lets the commander replace the main body's firepower with cavalry reconnaissance
explanation: Page 54 says cavalry, by its role, is an economy of force with flexible capabilities that let the commander conserve combat power for engagement where he desires.

prompt: Which pair lists capabilities of tanks?
options: Operate in an economy of force role; conduct reconnaissance and surveillance
Destroy light armor vehicles; maneuver with tanks
Secure terrain; assault unprepared, suppressed defenses
Operate in an opposed entry role; use strategic and tactical mobility to advantage
explanation: Page 66 lists operating in an opposed entry role and using strategic and tactical mobility to advantage as tank capabilities. The other pairs belong to cavalry (page 60) and mounted mechanized infantry (page 28).

prompt: Which list gives the planning considerations for tanks?
options: Surface danger zone, direct fire control measures, where to dismount troops, cover against enemy air
Surface danger zone, direct fire control measures, SBF positions, distance from main body
Surface danger zone, direct fire control measures, SBF positions, cover against enemy air
Direct fire control measures, SBF positions, security operations, cover against enemy air
explanation: Page 71 lists the tank considerations: surface danger zone, direct fire control measures, SBF positions, cover against enemy air, and use against other tanks or armored vehicles. Where to dismount is a mechanized infantry item (page 69); distance from main body and security operations are cavalry items (page 70).

prompt: Which list gives the planning considerations for cavalry?
options: Indirect fire weapon support, weapon range, security operations, distance from main body
Indirect fire weapon support, weapon range, security operations, surface danger zone
Indirect fire weapon support, weapon range, where to dismount troops, distance from main body
Weapon range, objective to combat trains distance, security operations, distance from main body
explanation: Page 70 lists the cavalry considerations: indirect fire weapon support, weapon range, security operations, distance from main body, and no use against tank units. Surface danger zone is a tank item (page 71); where to dismount and objective to combat trains distance are mechanized infantry items (page 69).

category: Major Equipment of the Armor Division
prompt: What are the maximum effective range and maximum range of the Browning M2 heavy barrel on the basic M113A2?
explanation: Page 73 gives the basic M113A2's Browning M2 heavy barrel 1,830 m maximum effective and 6,800 m maximum range. 1,700 m and 2,000 m are the RCWS M2A1 QCB (page 74), 3,000 m is the 25 mm cannon, and 1,100 m and 3,725 m are the M60.

category: Major Equipment of the Armor Division
prompt: Which of the following describes the main gun of the Sabrah Light Tank?
options: A 76 mm L23A1 gun with a 2,200 m direct-fire effective range
A 105 mm gun with a 3,600 m combat effective range, firing 6 rounds per minute
A 105 mm gun with a 2,200 m combat effective range, firing 6 rounds per minute
A 76 mm gun with a 3,600 m combat effective range, firing 40 rounds per minute
explanation: Page 82 gives the Sabrah a 105 mm gun with a 3,600 m combat effective range and 6 rounds per minute. The 76 mm L23A1 with 2,200 m direct fire belongs to the Fire Support Vehicle (page 81).

prompt: A battalion commander passes orders by radio to every vehicle at once while his company commanders coordinate fire and movement on the move. This describes which characteristic of armor?
options: Flexibility
Intensive and flexible communication
Mobility
Shock action
explanation: Page 20 lists intensive and flexible communication as a characteristic of armor; passing and coordinating orders by radio is what the scenario shows, not a change of task (flexibility).

prompt: Which limitation belongs to mechanized infantry and not to cavalry or tanks?
options: Dismounted infantrymen are vulnerable to small arms and indirect fire
High logistics requirements
Dependence on flatbeds for deployment to the theater
Mobility and firepower restricted in extremely close terrain
explanation: Page 30 lists dismounted infantrymen's vulnerability to small arms and indirect fire as a mechanized infantry limitation. High logistics requirements is a cavalry limitation (page 61); flatbeds and close terrain are tank limitations (pages 67-68).

prompt: Which weapon handling rules are prescribed by the SOPs on dismounting and on mounting, respectively?
options: Chamber empty, muzzle up; clear weapons and muzzle up
Chamber loaded, muzzle down; clear weapons and muzzle down
Chamber empty, muzzle down; keep weapons loaded, muzzle up
Chamber empty, muzzle down; clear weapons and muzzle down
explanation: Page 31 (dismounting) requires chamber empty, muzzle down. Page 45 (mounting) requires that once inside the AV, weapons are cleared and muzzles pointed down.

prompt: Which of the following SOPs applies to mounting but NOT to dismounting?
options: No riders on top of the AV
Never hide behind an AV
First to dismount is the last to mount, and vice versa
Provide cover while others are mounting
explanation: Page 45 lists providing cover while others are mounting as a mounting SOP. The other three are dismounting SOPs on page 31.

prompt: Which capability is listed for CAVALRY and not for tanks or mechanized infantry?
options: Operate in an opposed entry role
Use thermal sights to enhance night fighting
Operate in an economy of force role without being reinforced
Destroy light armor vehicles while mounted
explanation: Page 60 says cavalry can operate in an economy of force role without being reinforced in offensive, defensive or delay operations. Opposed entry and thermal sights are tank capabilities (page 66); destroying light armor vehicles is a mounted mechanized infantry capability (page 28).

prompt: In the tank platoon chart, which rank is shown for the platoon sergeant?
options: TSG
MSG
SSG
SGT
explanation: Page 65 shows the platoon leader as LT, the platoon sergeant as TSG and the two other tank commanders as SSG.

prompt: Infantry units lack the organic transportation to support tank CSS needs, especially in which classes of supply?
options: Classes III, V and IX
Classes I, III and V
Classes II, IV and VIII
Classes III, VII and IX
explanation: Page 68 says infantry units do not have the organic transportation assets to support tank CSS needs, especially Classes III, V and IX.

prompt: In the tank planning considerations, SBF positions stands for:
options: Security and blocking force positions
Secure the battle frontage positions
Support by fire positions
Suppression by fire positions
explanation: Page 73 lists SBF (support by fire) positions among the tank planning considerations.

prompt: Which of these is listed among the planning considerations of both mechanized infantry and cavalry?
options: Surface danger zone
Distance from main body
Weapon range
Avenue of approach restrictions
explanation: Pages 69 and 70 list weapon range as item 2 for both mechanized infantry and cavalry. Surface danger zone is tank only (page 71), distance from main body is cavalry only, and avenue of approach restrictions is mechanized infantry only.

category: Major Equipment of the Armor Division
prompt: Which of the following is the 25 mm primary cannon of the AIFV?
options: Oerlikon KBA
Bushmaster MK-44
Ordnance L23A1
Browning M2A1 QCB
explanation: Page 76 gives the AIFV the 25 mm Oerlikon KBA. The Bush-Master MK-44 is the M113A2 UTS cannon (page 75), the L23A1 is the 76 mm FSV gun, and the M2A1 QCB is the RCWS weapon.

category: Major Equipment of the Armor Division
prompt: Which list gives the meanings of ATT, FCS and EDS in the M113A2 Remote Controlled Weapon System?
options: Automated Turret Traverse, Fire Coordination System, Electronic Defense System
Automatic Target Tracking, Fire Coordination System, Electronic Defense System
Automated Turret Traverse, Fire Control System, Electrical Drive System
Automatic Target Tracking, Fire Control System, Electrical Drive System
explanation: Page 74 gives Automatic Target Tracking (ATT), Fire Control System (FCS) and Electrical Drive System (EDS).

category: Major Equipment of the Armor Division
prompt: Which of the following describes the Simba Fighting Vehicle?
options: Front wheel drive, one-man turret, run flat tires, fully amphibious
Aluminum alloy hull, full tracked laying, fully amphibious, troop or cargo carrier
Cummins ISC diesel engine, crew of 3 plus 7 passengers, acquired in 2024 under Horizon 2
Armored monocoque hull, two or four wheel drive, air conditioned, 0.43 m vertical obstacle
explanation: Page 80 gives the Simba an armored monocoque hull, two or four wheel drive, air conditioning and a 0.43 m maximum vertical obstacle. The others describe the V-150S (page 79), the M113A2 (page 73) and the Guarani (page 83).

category: Major Equipment of the Armor Division
prompt: Which of the following describes the Mounted Mortar System (MMS) on the M113A2?
options: 81/120 mm smooth bore, muzzle loaded, self-propelled, recoiling mortar for small and medium sized vehicles
81/120 mm smooth bore, breech loaded, self-propelled, recoiling mortar for small and medium sized vehicles
81/120 mm rifled, muzzle loaded, self-propelled, recoiling mortar for small and medium sized vehicles
81/120 mm smooth bore, muzzle loaded, towed, recoiling mortar for small and medium sized vehicles
explanation: Page 77 describes the MMS as an 81 mm/120 mm smooth bore, muzzle loaded, self-propelled, recoiling mortar designed for installation on small and medium sized vehicles.

prompt: An armor unit is tasked to neutralize an enemy force by fire, maneuver and shock effect in coordination with other arms. Which armor sub-component is being employed?
options: Tank operations
Mechanized infantry operations
Cavalry operations
Fire support vehicle operations
explanation: Pages 15 and 17 give the tank mission as neutralizing enemy forces by fire, maneuver and shock effect in coordination with other units. Mechanized infantry closes to destroy or capture (page 18); cavalry performs reconnaissance, surveillance and security (page 16).

category: Major Equipment of the Armor Division
prompt: The M113A2 Armored Personnel Carrier data sheet lists which electrical system and radio?
options: 24 V DC; RF 5800 HH Harris vehicular radio
12 V DC; RF 5800 HH Harris vehicular radio
24 V DC; BMS and Navigation System
12 V DC; BMS and Navigation System
explanation: Page 73 lists a 24 V DC electrical system and the RF 5800 HH Harris vehicular radio. The BMS and Navigation System appear on the Sabrah sheet (page 82).
